title: Interview with David Tester VP of Engineering Mach42
gist: Interview with Mach42 VP of Engineering David Tester: Mach42 replaces hand-written Verilog-A analog models with ML-trained neural network surrogates that stay within a few percent of transistor-level accuracy while simulating orders of magnitude faster, letting teams expand pre-silicon signoff simulation instead of the brute-force compute approach.

insights.claim: In analog IC design, hand-written Verilog-A models are often not maintained or fail to capture detailed circuit behaviour, so subsystem and full-chip simulations fall back to slow pre-layout schematic views, limiting their scope.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Analog verification remains a compute and schedule bottleneck ripe for ML tooling.
insights.locator: For many years, analog IC design

insights.claim: After layout, the gap between hand-written Verilog-A models and post-layout extracted views widens further, and full-chip signoff simulations on extracted views run even slower.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Post-layout signoff is where acceleration value is greatest.

insights.claim: Product complexity is now so high that silicon respins can devastate the commercial case for many products.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Raises willingness to pay for pre-silicon verification tools.
insights.quote: product complexity is so challenging now that the impact of silicon respins can devastate the commercial case for many products

insights.claim: Mach42 replaces hand-written Verilog-A models with machine-generated neural network models trained on schematic circuit simulations, retaining detailed circuit behaviour with accuracy within a few percent of the actual design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: ML surrogates could displace manual behavioural modelling in analog flows.
insights.locator: Mach42 is pursuing a different approach

insights.claim: David Tester claims Mach42's ML-generated models are as accurate as transistor-level simulations yet simulate orders of magnitude faster, letting teams drastically increase the number and complexity of chip signoff simulations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If validated, a meaningful productivity shift in analog/mixed-signal signoff with implications for EDA incumbents.
insights.quote: the Mach42 models generated by ML are just as accurate as transistor-level simulations, but they simulate orders of magnitude faster

insights.claim: Mach42 positions itself as AI infrastructure enabling current and future AI-based orchestration solutions to explore designs in greater depth and coverage in shorter time frames.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fast surrogates are an enabling layer for agentic design exploration.

themes.theme: Expand pre-silicon scope, not brute force

insights.claim: The prevailing industry approach to analog verification is brute force: limiting signoff simulation ambition under schedule pressure and throwing more CPU at 100% transistor-level runs that already use top-end machines.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Highlights diminishing returns of compute-only scaling in analog EDA.

insights.claim: David Tester argues the best way to de-risk developments and launch on schedule is to increase the scope of pre-silicon simulations, not decrease it, yet complexity and tight timelines create pressure to cut that scope.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Demand for pre-silicon verification capacity should grow with chip complexity.
insights.quote: the best way to de-risk developments and launch products on schedule is to increase the scope of pre-silicon simulations, not decrease it
